Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $f:X\to S$ be a finite morphism of schemes.
Then every ring map $A\to B$ induced by $f$ on an affine chart
$U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq S$ with $f^{-1}(U)=\operatorname{Spec}B$ is
integral. Moreover $f$ is universally closed: for every morphism $T\to S$ the
base-changed projection $X\times_ST\to T$ is a closed map, so the image of
$X\times_ST$ and of every closed subset of it is closed in $|T|$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice.

Let $f:A\to B$ be an integral ring map, and let $\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ with $\ker f\subseteq\mathfrak p$. Then there exists a prime ideal $\mathfrak q\in\operatorname{Spec}(B)$ such that $f^{-1}(\mathfrak q)=\mathfrak p$.

Let $k$ be a field and let $A$ be a nonzero finite-type $k$-algebra. Then
there exist algebraically independent elements $z_1,\ldots,z_d\in A$ such that
$A$ is a module-finite algebra over the polynomial ring
$k[z_1,\ldots,z_d]$.

If $X$ is an irreducible classical variety, then $\dim X=\operatorname{trdeg}_k k(X)<\infty$.

Work over a fixed algebraically closed field $k$, with the Axiom of Choice. Classical varieties are separated and admit finite affine covers; they may be reducible or empty unless irreducibility is specified. Irreducible means nonempty. All fibres and points below are classical closed-point fibres and points.

Let $k$ be a field, let $A$ be a finite-type $k$-domain, and let $K=\operatorname{Frac}(A)$. Then
$$ \dim A=\operatorname{trdeg}_k K. $$

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $k$ be a field, let $A$ be a finite-type $k$-domain, and let $\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Spec}(A)$. Then
$$ \operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak p)+\operatorname{trdeg}_k\operatorname{Frac}(A/\mathfrak p)=\operatorname{trdeg}_k\operatorname{Frac}(A). $$

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $R$ be a Noetherian commutative ring, let
$$ I=(x_1,\ldots,x_n) $$
be an ideal generated by $n\ge1$ elements, and let $\mathfrak p$ be a prime ideal minimal over $I$. Then $\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak p)\le n$.

If $U$ is a nonempty open of an irreducible classical variety $X$, then $\dim U=\dim X$. Every proper closed subvariety $Z\subsetneq X$ has $\dim Z<\dim X$.

Let $k$ be a field and let $C$ be a reduced $k$-scheme of finite type, of pure
dimension one (for example a reduced projective plane curve or an open
subscheme of one). Then there exists a finite morphism
$\nu\colon C^{\mathrm{nu}}\to C$ with the following properties:

1. $C^{\mathrm{nu}}$ is regular of dimension one (equivalently normal: all
   local rings are discrete valuation rings or fields);
2. $\nu$ is an isomorphism over the regular locus of $C$ and is birational on
   each irreducible component;
3. on an affine chart $\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $C$, $\nu$ is the morphism
   corresponding to the integral closure of $A$ in its total ring of
   fractions;
4. $\nu$ is unique up to a unique $C$-isomorphism, and $\nu_*\mathcal O_{C^{\mathrm{nu}}}$
   is a coherent $\mathcal O_C$-module.

No separability or perfectness hypothesis on $k$ is needed.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $k$ be a perfect
field and let $X$ be a finite-type $k$-scheme. Here **regular** means that $X$
is locally Noetherian and every local ring $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ is regular local;
**smooth over $k$** means that $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is smooth under the
local-standard-smooth convention of
[[def-smooth-morphism-classical]]. Then
$$X\text{ is regular}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad X\to\operatorname{Spec}k\text{ is smooth}.$$
No reducedness, irreducibility, or closed-point restriction is imposed.

Let $C$ be a complex algebraic curve, meaning a one-dimensional algebraic set
over $\mathbb C$ ([[def-affine-algebraic-set]]), and let $p\in C$ lie either in
$\mathbb C^N$ (affine case) or in a standard affine chart of $\mathbb{CP}^N$
with its coordinates $(\zeta_1/\zeta_i,\dots)$ (projective case,
[[def-projective-space-points]]). Assume that near $p$ the curve is the common
zero set of holomorphic functions $f_1,\dots,f_{N-1}$ on a neighbourhood of $p$,
and that their complex Jacobian matrix at $p$ has rank $N-1$. Here the
matrix $J_F(p)=(\partial f_i/\partial t_j(p))$ uses the equation-row and
coordinate-column convention of
[[def-jacobian-matrix-affine-algebraic-set]], extended directly to the stated
local holomorphic functions by their complex partial derivatives; this hypothesis is the
**Jacobian-rank sense** of nonsingularity used in this pair.

Then there are an index $j$, a plane domain $A\subseteq\mathbb C$ and a
holomorphic map $\phi:A\to\mathbb C^{N-1}$ such that, after permuting the
coordinates so that the $j$-th coordinate comes first,
$C$ agrees near $p$ with the graph $\{(z,\phi(z)):z\in A\}$, and the projection
$(z,\phi(z))\mapsto z$ is a homeomorphism of that neighbourhood of $p$ in $C$
onto the plane domain $A$ whose inverse $z\mapsto(z,\phi(z))$ is holomorphic:
one free ambient coordinate is a local parameter. Moreover, if two such local
parameters $z$ and $w$ are defined on overlapping pieces, coming from the same
ambient chart or from two standard affine charts, then the transition
$z\mapsto w$ is holomorphic wherever both are defined.

Let $m,n\ge1$, let $U\subseteq\mathbb C^m\times\mathbb C^n$ be open, let
$f:U\to\mathbb C^n$ be holomorphic, and let $(a,b)\in U$ satisfy $f(a,b)=0$.
Assume the complex Jacobian with respect to the second block is invertible:

$$\det\left(\frac{\partial f_j}{\partial w_k}(a,b)\right)_{1\le j,k\le n}\ne0.$$

Then there are neighbourhoods $A$ of $a$ and $B$ of $b$, and a unique
holomorphic map $\varphi:A\to B$, such that

$$f(z,\varphi(z))=0\qquad(z\in A),$$

and, after shrinking $A\times B$ if needed,

$$f(z,w)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad w=\varphi(z).$$

Let $k$ be any field, let $n\geq0$ be finite, let $I$ be an ideal of
$k[t_1,\ldots,t_n]$, and put
$$X=\operatorname{Spec}(k[t_1,\ldots,t_n]/I).$$
Let $a=(a_1,\ldots,a_n)\in X(k)$, and let
$f_1,\ldots,f_r$ be any finite generating list of the actual ideal $I$.
Then the coordinate-velocity map gives a canonical $k$-linear isomorphism
$$T_aX\cong\ker\!\left(J_{(f_1,\ldots,f_r)}(a):k^n\longrightarrow k^r\right).$$
The kernel is independent of the chosen finite generating list of $I$. No
reducedness, perfectness, or characteristic hypothesis is needed. Finiteness of
the list is available for every finite $n$ by the finite-variable polynomial
Noetherian result cited below.

Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian scheme and $x\in X$. Write
$R=\mathcal O_{X,x}$, let $\mathfrak m_x$ be its maximal ideal, and set
$\kappa(x)=R/\mathfrak m_x$. The point $x$ is **regular** when $R$ is a
regular local ring, with regularity defined by
$\operatorname{edim}R=\dim R$. Then the intrinsic tangent space $T_xX$ is
finite-dimensional over $\kappa(x)$, and
$$x\text{ is regular}\Longleftrightarrow\dim_{\kappa(x)}T_xX=\dim\mathcal O_{X,x}.$$
This is absolute regularity of the local ring; it asserts no smoothness over a
base field.

Assume the Axiom of Choice.

Every nonzero commutative Noetherian local ring $R$ satisfies $\dim R\le\operatorname{edim}R<\infty$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). A regular local ring $R$ of dimension $d$ is a domain and Cohen–Macaulay. For every regular system $(x_1,\ldots,x_d)$, the tuple is $R$-regular and $R/(x_1,\ldots,x_c)$ is regular local of dimension $d-c$ for all $0\le c\le d$.

Let $R$ be a Noetherian commutative ring. Then the polynomial ring $R[x]$ is a
Noetherian commutative ring.

No hypothesis beyond Noetherianity is placed on $R$: it may have zero divisors,
and it may be the zero ring.

Classical varieties are separated and admit finite affine covers; they may be reducible or empty unless irreducibility is specified. Irreducible means nonempty. The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

Let $X$ be a reduced quasi-projective complex algebraic variety, regarded as a
classical variety over $\mathbb C$
([[def-classical-algebraic-prevariety-regular-maps-and-varieties]]) with its
analytic topology, its smooth points (regular local rings) and its finite
smooth algebraic frontier stratifications
([[def-analytic-topology-and-finite-smooth-algebraic-stratifications]]).

(a) **Whitney conditions.** Let $X=\coprod_{\alpha\in A}S_\alpha$ be a finite smooth algebraic frontier stratification whose strata are pure-dimensional, and let $R\subseteq\overline S\setminus S$ be incident strata. In local analytic charts of an ambient smooth manifold, the pair $(S,R)$ satisfies **Whitney (a)** at $y\in R$ if for every sequence $x_n\in S$ with $x_n\to y$ whose tangent planes $T_{x_n}S$ converge to a plane $T$, one has $T_yR\subseteq T$; it satisfies **Whitney (b)** at $y$ if additionally, whenever $y_n\in R$ with $y_n\to y$ and the real secant lines through $x_n,y_n$ converge to a line $\ell$, one has $\ell\subseteq T$. A **finite complex algebraic Whitney stratification** of $X$ is a finite smooth algebraic frontier stratification satisfying (a) and (b) at every point of every incident pair. Coordinate independence of the limits and the implication (b)$\Rightarrow$(a), commonly used in the literature, are not assumed as proved here; requiring both conditions makes the intended interface explicit.

(b) **Tube control data.** A system of **tube control data** on the analytic stratified space $X$ consists of an open neighbourhood $T_R$ of each stratum $R$, a continuous retraction $\pi_R:T_R\to R$ and a continuous radius $\rho_R:T_R\to[0,\infty)$ such that $\rho_R^{-1}(0)=R$, both maps are smooth on each stratum, and for every incident upper stratum $S$ the pair $(\pi_R,\rho_R)$ restricts to a submersion $S\cap T_R\to R\times(0,\infty)$. On the overlap neighbourhoods where the compositions are defined one requires $\pi_R\pi_S=\pi_R$ and $\rho_R\pi_S=\rho_R$ for $R<S$; every compatibility assertion must name the common domain on which the composition is defined. Tubes may be shrunk. For local conical constructions one requires local properness over compact base slices: sufficiently small closed radius ranges over a compact neighbourhood in $R$ have compact inverse image inside the tube.

(c) **$f$-compatible tubes and controlled lifts.** Let $f:W\to B$ be a stratified submersion onto a smooth manifold. A tube system is **$f$-compatible** if $f\pi_R=f$ on the tubes used. A **controlled lift** of a smooth base field $v$ on $B$ is a field $V$ that is smooth on each stratum and satisfies $df(V)=v\circ f$, $d\pi_R(V)=V|_R\circ\pi_R$ and $d\rho_R(V)=0$ on specified controlled tube neighbourhoods. **Locally bounded** means the ambient norm is bounded on a neighbourhood of every point; this is an additional hypothesis, not a consequence of the definition. **Radial controlled lifts** instead satisfy $d\rho_R(V)=\rho_R$ with fixed $\pi_R$ together with the appropriate annular overlap controls.

(d) **Conical product neighbourhoods.** A **conical product neighbourhood along $R$** is a stratum-preserving homeomorphism from a neighbourhood of a point of $R$ to $B^{2\dim_{\mathbb C}R}\times c(L)$ carrying $R$ to the ball times the cone apex, with compact finitely Whitney-stratified $L$. The radial and tangential transports must be compatible with the actual coefficient data when cohomological local systems are deduced; topological existence alone does not supply canonical derived-sheaf transport.

(e) **Finite triangulation of a noncompact space.** In the compactification convention used here, a **finite triangulation** of a noncompact space $X$ consists of finite simplicial complexes $D\subseteq K$ together with a homeomorphism $|K|\setminus|D|\to X$; compatibility with prescribed subsets means they are unions of interiors of retained simplices. This does not assert that algebraic morphisms become simplicial, and real simplicial dimensions do not replace the complex dimensions of the algebraic strata.

Fix an algebraically closed field $k$. The affine models used here are polynomial zero sets $Z\subseteq k^n$, including empty and reducible sets. Their closed subsets are common zero loci of polynomial families, relative to $Z$. Intersections combine equations, and finite unions use products of equations, so these are the closed sets of a topology.

For an open $U\subseteq Z$, let $\mathcal O_Z(U)$ consist of functions $U\to k$ locally equal to $a/b$ for polynomials $a,b$ with $b$ nonvanishing on the chosen neighbourhood. Pointwise operations and restriction make these sets a sheaf of $k$-algebras: quotient expressions persist on restriction, and functions that agree locally glue uniquely with the same local quotient property. At a point z its stalk is the ring of germs of such functions. Evaluation at z maps it onto k, with kernel the germs vanishing at z. A germ nonzero at z is invertible: shrink to where its numerator and denominator are both nonzero and interchange them. Thus the kernel is the unique maximal ideal. These affine models are locally ringed spaces in the sense of [[def-locally-ringed-space]], with residue fields canonically k.

A **classical algebraic prevariety** over k is a quasi-compact locally ringed space with a structure sheaf of k-algebras, covered by open subspaces isomorphic over k to these affine models. Here quasi-compact means every open cover has a finite subcover. Equivalently it admits a finite affine-model cover. To justify the converse, each affine model is quasi-compact: polynomial principal opens $D_Z(h)=\{z:h(z)\ne0\}$ form a basis. Given an open cover, take all h whose principal opens lie in a member. $\alpha$ near $a$ and $\beta$ near $F(a)$ such that

$$\beta\circ F\circ \alpha^{-1}(u,v)=(u,0)$$

for $(u,v)\in\mathbb C^r\times\mathbb C^{m-r}$ near $0$. Empty blocks are
omitted when $r=0$, $r=m$, or $r=n$.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

derivations.claim: We record a partition construction. Let $Z$ be a reduced separated complex algebraic variety of finite type and let $\mathcal C$ be a finite list of closed subsets of $Z$. There is a finite partition of $Z$ into irreducible smooth locally closed strata such that every member of $\mathcal C$ is a union of strata and every stratum is open dense in its own irreducible closure. If $Z=\varnothing$ take the empty partition. Otherwise let $Z_1,\ldots,Z_m$ be the irreducible components of $Z$, finitely many by [F1]. Remove from $Z_i$ its nonsmooth locus, the other components $Z_j$, and every $C\cap Z_i$ with $C\in\mathcal C$ and $C\nsupseteq Z_i$. Each removed set is closed, and each is proper in the irreducible $Z_i$; by [F3] and [F2] the nonsmooth locus has smaller dimension, and by [F2] the other removed sets do too, so the result $U_i$ is a nonempty dense open subset of $Z_i$ and is contained in or disjoint from every $C\in\mathcal C$. The $U_i$ are pairwise disjoint and open in $Z$, because their complement is the finite union of the removed closed sets and the sets $Z_j$ with $j\ne i$. The remainder $Z':=Z\setminus\bigcup_iU_i$ is closed and meets each $Z_i$ in a proper closed subset, so $\dim Z'<\dim Z$ by [F2]. Partition $Z'$ by the same construction with $\mathcal C$ replaced by the restrictions of all members of $\mathcal C$ and of all $Z_i$ to $Z'$, and iterate. The dimension of the remainder strictly decreases at every round, so the recursion terminates; because each round respects the restricted lists, every member of $\mathcal C$ is a union of strata and every stratum is open dense in its irreducible closure.

Now construct the target strata in rounds on a closed residual subvariety $R\subseteq Y$, starting with $R=Y$; at each stage keep finite lists of prescribed closed subsets of $R$ and of $f^{-1}(R)$, initially the given lists and later those lists enlarged by the restrictions of the closures of all previously emitted strata. Apply step 1.1 to $f^{-1}(R)$ with the maintained source list, obtaining a finite partition into irreducible smooth locally closed strata $Z_\alpha$. Fix an irreducible component $R_i$ of $R$ and remove from it its nonsmooth locus, the other components of $R$, and every maintained target prescribed closed subset not containing $R_i$; by [F1] this leaves a nonempty dense open subset $V_i^0\subseteq R_i$. For each $\alpha$ the image $f(Z_\alpha)$ is irreducible and lies in a component of $R$, so its closure in $R$ is an irreducible closed subset of some component. If that closure is not $R_i$, then its intersection with $R_i$ is a proper closed subset, and we remove it from $V_i^0$; if the closure equals $R_i$, then $f|_{Z_\alpha}$ is dominant, $Z_\alpha$ is smooth and irreducible, and [F4] supplies a dense open subset of $R_i$ over which $Z_\alpha\to R_i$ is smooth, with nonempty fibres over the closed points after shrinking to lie in the image. There are finitely many $\alpha$, so intersecting $V_i^0$ with all these dense opens (and with the images) produces a nonempty dense open $V_i\subseteq R_i$ such that every $Z_\alpha$ whose image closure is not $R_i$ has no point over $V_i$, while every $Z_\alpha$ whose image closure is $R_i$ maps smoothly and onto $V_i$.

Emit the target strata $V_i$ of this round and, for every $\alpha$ whose $Z_\alpha$ maps onto $R_i$, the source stratum $S_{\alpha,i}:=Z_\alpha\cap f^{-1}(V_i)$, which is nonempty. It is open in $Z_\alpha$ because $V_i$ is open in $R_i$ and $Z_\alpha\subseteq f^{-1}(R_i)$, hence it is an irreducible smooth locally closed subvariety of $X$, and it maps smoothly and onto $V_i$ as the restriction of the map of step 2.1. Every source point over $V_i$ lies in exactly one such stratum, because the $Z_\alpha$ partition $f^{-1}(R)$ and each $Z_\alpha$ is contained in or disjoint from $f^{-1}(V_i)$. Within the round, closures behave as in step 1.1: the closure of $S_{\alpha,i}$ meets $f^{-1}(V_i)$ in the union of the strata $S_{\beta,i}$ with $Z_\beta\subseteq\overline{Z_\alpha}$, since $f^{-1}(V_i)$ is open in the closed set $f^{-1}(R_i)$.

Put $R':=R\setminus\bigcup_iV_i$; it is closed and has $\dim R'<\dim R$ by [F2], since each component of $R$ lost a dense open subset. Enlarge both lists by the closures of the emitted strata, restrict to $R'$ and $f^{-1}(R')$, and repeat steps 2.1 and 3.1. The target dimension strictly decreases each round, so after finitely many rounds the emitted strata partition $Y$ and $X$. Every emitted stratum $S$ is open dense in its irreducible closure: this holds within each round by step 3.1, because the pieces of the frontier partition whose closures contain $S$ are contained in $\overline S$ and dense in it; and the maintained lists, which contain the closure of $S$ in every later round, force every later stratum to be contained in or disjoint from $\overline S$. Consequently $\overline S$ is a union of strata, and every stratum $P\subseteq\overline S\setminus S$ has $\dim P<\dim S$: indeed $\overline P$ is an irreducible closed subset of $\overline S$ with $\dim\overline P\le\dim S$, equality would give $\overline P=\overline S$, and then $P$ and $S$, being dense opens of the irreducible $\overline P=\overline S$, would meet, contradicting disjointness of strata. Thus every stratum closure is a union of strata of no larger dimension and its boundary has strictly smaller dimension. Every prescribed subset is a union of strata by the invariance maintained in steps 1.1 and 2.1, and the empty source contributes no source strata.

Finally let $S\to T$ be one emitted restriction onto a target stratum. The stratum $S$ is a smooth complex variety by construction, so by [F3] it is locally standard smooth over $\mathbb C$; the defining equations of a standard smooth presentation near a point have an invertible Jacobian minor, and [F5] turns them into holomorphic charts of $S$ near that point, with holomorphic transition maps. Similarly $T$ carries holomorphic charts. The map $S\to T$ is a morphism of classical varieties, so in these charts its components are restrictions of regular functions on affine charts, hence polynomial in the ambient coordinates and therefore holomorphic in the chart parameters. At every point the differential of $S\to T$ is surjective by the smoothness of the restriction and the criterion of [F5]; since surjectivity onto a target of dimension $n$ is the nonvanishing of some $n\times n$ minor, the rank stays full on a neighbourhood, and the holomorphic constant rank theorem exhibits the map near each point as a linear projection in suitable holomorphic coordinates. Hence the restriction is a submersion of complex manifolds, in particular a submersion of the underlying real smooth manifolds. No properness or topological triviality is used, and AC is inherited exactly through the cited suppliers.

boundaries.evidence: The Statement explicitly allows the empty source: step 2.1 still stratifies the target, and step 3.1 emits no source stratum because no component $Z_alpha$ exists.

boundaries.reason: The rounds of step 4.1 compare dimensions and never divide by one; a zero-dimensional residual component simply contributes a last stratum rather than a special case.
No singleton or one-round hypothesis occurs; step 2.1 runs the round construction until the target residual is empty, for any finite number of rounds.
Strata are open subsets of regular loci, so there is no degenerate stratum parameter; singular points stay in the continuing residual and are stratified in later rounds.
No interval or asymptotic endpoint appears; strip closures are recorded as finite set-theoretic frontiers in steps 2.1 and 4.1.

boundaries.evidence: The Statement assumes AC, consumed through the regular-locus and dimension suppliers [F3] and [F4] in steps 1.1 and 2.1; each round selects only from finite lists of components and strata.

citations.quote:
Let $X$ be a reduced quasi-projective complex algebraic variety, regarded as a
classical variety over $\mathbb C$
([[def-classical-algebraic-prevariety-regular-maps-and-varieties]]) with its
analytic topology, its smooth points (regular local rings) and its finite
smooth algebraic frontier stratifications
([[def-analytic-topology-and-finite-smooth-algebraic-stratifications]]).

(a) **Whitney conditions.** Let $X=\coprod_{\alpha\in A}S_\alpha$ be a finite smooth algebraic frontier stratification whose strata are pure-dimensional, and let $R\subseteq\overline S\setminus S$ be incident strata. In local analytic charts of an ambient smooth manifold, the pair $(S,R)$ satisfies **Whitney (a)** at $y\in R$ if for every sequence $x_n\in S$ with $x_n\to y$ whose tangent planes $T_{x_n}S$ converge to a plane $T$, one has $T_yR\subseteq T$; it satisfies **Whitney (b)** at $y$ if additionally, whenever $y_n\in R$ with $y_n\to y$ and the real secant lines through $x_n,y_n$ converge to a line $\ell$, one has $\ell\subseteq T$. A **finite complex algebraic Whitney stratification** of $X$ is a finite smooth algebraic frontier stratification satisfying (a) and (b) at every point of every incident pair. Coordinate independence of the limits and the implication (b)$\Rightarrow$(a), commonly used in the literature, are not assumed as proved here; requiring both conditions makes the intended interface explicit.

(b) **Tube control data.** A system of **tube control data** on the analytic stratified space $X$ consists of an open neighbourhood $T_R$ of each stratum $R$, a continuous retraction $\pi_R:T_R\to R$ and a continuous radius $\rho_R:T_R\to[0,\infty)$ such that $\rho_R^{-1}(0)=R$, both maps are smooth on each stratum, and for every incident upper stratum $S$ the pair $(\pi_R,\rho_R)$ restricts to a submersion $S\cap T_R\to R\times(0,\infty)$. On the overlap neighbourhoods where the compositions are defined one requires $\pi_R\pi_S=\pi_R$ and $\rho_R\pi_S=\rho_R$ for $R<S$; every compatibility assertion must name the common domain on which the composition is defined. Tubes may be shrunk. For local conical constructions one requires local properness over compact base slices: sufficiently small closed radius ranges over a compact neighbourhood in $R$ have compact inverse image inside the tube.

(c) **$f$-compatible tubes and controlled lifts.** Let $f:W\to B$ be a stratified submersion onto a smooth manifold. A tube system is **$f$-compatible** if $f\pi_R=f$ on the tubes used. A **controlled lift** of a smooth base field $v$ on $B$ is a field $V$ that is smooth on each stratum and satisfies $df(V)=v\circ f$, $d\pi_R(V)=V|_R\circ\pi_R$ and $d\rho_R(V)=0$ on specified controlled tube neighbourhoods. **Locally bounded** means the ambient norm is bounded on a neighbourhood of every point; this is an additional hypothesis, not a consequence of the definition. **Radial controlled lifts** instead satisfy $d\rho_R(V)=\rho_R$ with fixed $\pi_R$ together with the appropriate annular overlap controls.

(d) **Conical product neighbourhoods.** A **conical product neighbourhood along $R$** is a stratum-preserving homeomorphism from a neighbourhood of a point of $R$ to $B^{2\dim_{\mathbb C}R}\times c(L)$ carrying $R$ to the ball times the cone apex, with compact finitely Whitney-stratified $L$. The radial and tangential transports must be compatible with the actual coefficient data when cohomological local systems are deduced; topological existence alone does not supply canonical derived-sheaf transport.

(e) **Finite triangulation of a noncompact space.** In the compactification convention used here, a **finite triangulation** of a noncompact space $X$ consists of finite simplicial complexes $D\subseteq K$ together with a homeomorphism $|K|\setminus|D|\to X$; compatibility with prescribed subsets means they are unions of interiors of retained simplices. This does not assert that algebraic morphisms become simplicial, and real simplicial dimensions do not replace the complex dimensions of the algebraic strata.

Assume AC. Let $f:X\to Y$ be one morphism of reduced separated complex
algebraic varieties of finite type
([[def-classical-algebraic-prevariety-regular-maps-and-varieties]]), and
prescribe finitely many closed algebraic subsets of each. There are finite
partitions of $X$ and $Y$ into irreducible smooth locally closed algebraic
strata such that every prescribed subset is a union of strata, every stratum
closure is a union of strata of no larger dimension with its boundary of
strictly smaller dimension, and each source stratum maps surjectively and
smoothly onto one target stratum. On analytic spaces each such restriction is a
submersion. The source may be empty. This assertion imposes no Whitney
condition, conical control or topological triviality.

Every classical variety is Noetherian and has finitely many irreducible components. Every open or closed subvariety has a finite affine cover.

Work over a fixed algebraically closed field $k$, with the Axiom of Choice. Classical varieties are separated and admit finite affine covers; they may be reducible or empty unless irreducibility is specified. Irreducible means nonempty. All fibres and points below are classical closed-point fibres and points.

If $U$ is a nonempty open of an irreducible classical variety $X$, then $\dim U=\dim X$. Every proper closed subvariety $Z\subsetneq X$ has $\dim Z<\dim X$.

Work over a fixed algebraically closed field $k$, with the Axiom of Choice. Classical varieties are separated and admit finite affine covers; they may be reducible or empty unless irreducibility is specified. Irreducible means nonempty. All fibres and points below are classical closed-point fibres and points.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $k$ be a perfect field
([[def-perfect-field]]) and let $X$ be a reduced $k$-scheme of finite type over
$k$. Then:

1. the regular locus $X_{\mathrm{reg}}=\{x\in|X|:\mathcal O_{X,x}\text{ is a regular local ring}\}$
   ([[def-singular-and-regular-loci-variety]]) is open in $X$;
2. for every irreducible component $Z$ of $X$
   ([[def-irreducible-component-of-a-topological-space]]) the intersection
   $X_{\mathrm{reg}}\cap Z$ is a dense open subset of $Z$; in particular every
   irreducible component contains a nonempty dense open subset of points
   regular on $X$;
3. if $X\ne\varnothing$, then $X_{\mathrm{reg}}\ne\varnothing$.

No separatedness, irreducibility or equidimensionality hypothesis is imposed,
and $X$ may be empty, in which case the second clause is vacuous and the third
is not asserted.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $k$ be a perfect
field and let $X$ be a finite-type $k$-scheme. Here **regular** means that $X$
is locally Noetherian and every local ring $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ is regular local;
**smooth over $k$** means that $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is smooth under the
local-standard-smooth convention of
[[def-smooth-morphism-classical]]. Then
$$X\text{ is regular}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad X\to\operatorname{Spec}k\text{ is smooth}.$$
No reducedness, irreducibility, or closed-point restriction is imposed.

Assume AC. Let $S,Y\subseteq\mathbb C^n$ be disjoint irreducible smooth locally
closed complex algebraic varieties with $Y\subseteq\overline S$ and
$\dim Y<\dim S$. There is a proper closed algebraic subset $E\subsetneq Y$ such
that $(S,Y)$ satisfies Whitney (a) and (b) at every point of $Y\setminus E$.
Finite prescribed incident upper strata can be treated with one common
exceptional subset by taking a finite union. The same result holds in the
affine charts of a quasi-projective algebraic ambient manifold.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $k$ be an algebraically
closed field of characteristic $0$, let $X$ and $Y$ be irreducible classical
varieties over $k$
([[def-classical-algebraic-prevariety-regular-maps-and-varieties]]), and let
$f\colon X\to Y$ be a morphism of classical varieties. Assume $X$ is smooth
over $k$, that is, the structure morphism $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is smooth
in the locally-standard-smooth sense of [[def-smooth-morphism-classical]]
(equivalently, since $k$ is perfect, $X$ is regular). Then:

1. there is a dense open subvariety $U\subseteq Y$ such that the restriction
   $$f^{-1}(U)\longrightarrow U$$
   is a smooth morphism of finite-type $k$-schemes; when $f$ is not dominant
   one may take $U$ with $f^{-1}(U)=\varnothing$, the empty morphism being
   smooth;
2. if in addition $f$ is dominant, there is a nonempty open (hence dense)
   $V\subseteq U$ such that for every closed point $y\in V$ the
   scheme-theoretic fibre
   $$X_y=X\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}k(y)$$
   ([[def-scheme-theoretic-fibre]]) is nonempty, smooth over $k$, and of pure
   dimension $r=\dim X-\dim Y$.

Neither $Y$ nor $f$ is required to be smooth or flat, the fibres are not
required to be irreducible or connected, and no statement is made about the
size of $U$ or $V$. The characteristic-$0$ hypothesis enters through the
critical-locus dimension bound of
[[lem-critical-locus-image-dimension-bound]] in claim 1 and through the
perfectness of $k$; the failure of the target-open statement for a
non-smooth source and the positive-characteristic failure of the
corresponding source-side statement are recorded on the counterexample page of
this pair.

Assume AC. Let $f:X\to Y$ be one morphism of reduced separated complex
algebraic varieties of finite type
([[def-classical-algebraic-prevariety-regular-maps-and-varieties]]), and
prescribe finitely many closed algebraic subsets of each. There are finite
partitions of $X$ and $Y$ into irreducible smooth locally closed algebraic
strata such that every prescribed subset is a union of strata, every stratum
closure is a union of strata of no larger dimension with its boundary of
strictly smaller dimension, and each source stratum maps surjectively and
smoothly onto one target stratum. On analytic spaces each such restriction is a
submersion. The source may be empty. This assertion imposes no Whitney
condition, conical control or topological triviality.

Let $m,n\ge1$, let $U\subseteq\mathbb C^m\times\mathbb C^n$ be open, let
$f:U\to\mathbb C^n$ be holomorphic, and let $(a,b)\in U$ satisfy $f(a,b)=0$.
Assume the complex Jacobian with respect to the second block is invertible:

$$\det\left(\frac{\partial f_j}{\partial w_k}(a,b)\right)_{1\le j,k\le n}\ne0.$$

Then there are neighbourhoods $A$ of $a$ and $B$ of $b$, and a unique
holomorphic map $\varphi:A\to B$, such that

$$f(z,\varphi(z))=0\qquad(z\in A),$$

and, after shrinking $A\times B$ if needed,

$$f(z,w)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad w=\varphi(z).$$

Let $n \in \mathbb{N}$ with $n \ge 1$, let $\mathbb{R}^n$ be the set of functions
$n \to \mathbb{R}$ and let $d_2$ be the Euclidean metric on it
([[lem-metrics-on-rn]]). Then:

1. **Closed boxes are compact.** For reals $a_k \le b_k$ $(k < n)$ the box
   $Q = \{\, x \in \mathbb{R}^n : a_k \le x_k \le b_k \text{ for every } k < n \,\}$
   is a compact subset of $(\mathbb{R}^n, d_2)$ ([[def-metric-compactness]]).
2. **Heine-Borel.** A subset $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ is a compact subset of
   $(\mathbb{R}^n, d_2)$ if and only if $K$ is closed in $\mathbb{R}^n$
   ([[def-metric-topology]]) and bounded
   ([[def-metric-bounded-diameter]]).
3. **The real line.** A subset $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ is a compact subset of
   $(\mathbb{R}, d_{\mathbb{R}})$, the usual metric $d_{\mathbb{R}}(x,y) = |x-y|$
   ([[lem-real-line-is-a-metric-space]]), if and only if $K$ is closed in
   $\mathbb{R}$ and bounded.

**No choice principle is used.** The bisection below halves one coordinate at a
time and takes the **left** half whenever the left half still fails to be finitely
covered, the right half otherwise: a rule with two outcomes, decided by a
property of the box, not a selection. That is the whole reason the theorem is
available in ZF, while the general "complete and totally bounded implies compact"
([[thm-complete-and-totally-bounded-implies-compact]]) is not.

The hypothesis $n \ge 1$ is inherited from [[lem-metrics-on-rn]], which defines
$\mathbb{R}^n$ and its metrics only there; the last remark below records what
happens at $n = 0$.

Let $(X, \mathcal{T}_X)$ and $(Y, \mathcal{T}_Y)$ be topological spaces
([[def-topological-space]]), and let $\mathbb{R}$ carry its usual topology, the
metric topology of $d_{\mathbb{R}}(s,t) = |s-t|$
([[lem-real-line-is-a-metric-space]], [[def-metric-topology]],
[[def-metrizable-space]]). Then:

1. **Continuous images.** If $f : X \to Y$ is continuous
   ([[def-continuous-map-top]]) and $(X, \mathcal{T}_X)$ is compact
   ([[def-compact-space]]), then $f[X]$ is a compact subset of $Y$. More
   generally, if $K \subseteq X$ is a compact subset of $X$ then $f[K]$ is a
   compact subset of $Y$.
2. **Extreme values.** If $(X, \mathcal{T}_X)$ is compact and nonempty and
   $g : X \to \mathbb{R}$ is continuous, then $g[X]$ has a maximum and a minimum
   ([[def-max-min]]): there are $x_{\max}, x_{\min} \in X$ with
   $$g(x_{\min}) \;\le\; g(x) \;\le\; g(x_{\max}) \qquad \text{for every } x \in X .$$
3. **Compact to Hausdorff.** If $(X, \mathcal{T}_X)$ is compact, $(Y,
   \mathcal{T}_Y)$ is Hausdorff ([[def-hausdorff-space]]) and $f : X \to Y$ is a
   continuous bijection, then $f$ is a homeomorphism
   ([[def-homeomorphism-and-open-maps]]).

Nonemptiness in claim 2 is a hypothesis and not an oversight: for
$X = \varnothing$ the image is empty and has neither a maximum nor a minimum. **No
choice principle is used**: the one selection made below is over a finite index
set, where [[lem-finite-choice]] is a theorem of ZF.

For every $n \in \mathbb{N}$ ([[def-natural-numbers]]) and every family
$(X_k)_{k < n}$ of compact topological spaces ([[def-compact-space]],
[[def-topological-space]]), the product

$$\prod_{k < n} X_k$$

with the product topology ([[def-product-topology]]) is compact. In particular a
binary product $X \times Y$ of compact spaces is compact, and the empty product,
a one-point space, is compact.

**No choice principle is used beyond [[lem-finite-choice]]**, which is a theorem
of ZF. That is what separates the finite case from the arbitrary one, where the
Axiom of Choice is genuinely spent.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

derivations.claim: Replace every prescribed locally closed subset $A$ by the two prescribed closed subsets $\overline A$ and $\overline A\setminus A$; their difference recovers $A$, and it suffices to respect the resulting finite list of closed subsets. Refine the smooth-partition construction of [F2] to construct, for a closed residual variety $R$ together with a finite list of prescribed closed subsets and finitely many previously fixed smooth strata outside $R$ whose closures must be respected, a Whitney partition of $R$ compatible with all of them: take the irreducible components $R_i$ of $R$, remove their nonsmooth loci and their intersections with the other components, and remove every prescribed closed subset not containing $R_i$, obtaining dense smooth opens $L_i$; then for every previously fixed upper stratum $S$, remove $R_i\cap\overline S$ when $R_i\not\subseteq\overline S$, and when $R_i\subseteq\overline S$ use [F3] to remove the closure in $R_i$ of the exceptional subset of [F3], which is proper because it has dimension smaller than $\dim R_i$. Finitely many upper strata leave nonempty dense smooth opens $U_i\subseteq R_i$, and [F3] makes each $U_i$ Whitney-regular with every incident previously fixed upper stratum.

Emit the $U_i$ as strata, add their closures $R_i$ to the list of closed subsets to be respected, and recurse on the closed complement $R\setminus\bigcup_iU_i$, whose dimension drops because every component lost a dense open subset. The recursion terminates by induction on dimension, producing a finite partition of $R$ into smooth irreducible locally closed strata. Strata of the same round have no frontier relation, since each $U_i$ misses all other components $R_j$. Every pair of incident strata has its upper stratum emitted earlier, and when the lower stratum was emitted step 1.1 imposed Whitney (a) and (b) with that upper stratum; boundaries have strictly smaller dimension by [F2]. The respected closures make every stratum closure a union of strata. In a quasi-projective ambient space, cover it by finitely many affine coordinate charts and apply the affine-chart version of [F3]; a sequence in $R$ converging to a point meets only finitely many components of the chart intersections, so passing to a subsequence in one component reduces the conditions to the chart version. Thus Whitney partitions compatible with a finite list of closed sets and with fixed external upper strata exist.

Construct the map-compatible partitions by decreasing target residual dimension. Start with target residual $R=Y$ and source residual $f^{-1}(R)=X$, and at each later round maintain the original closed-set lists together with the closures of all previously emitted source and target strata. Partition the source residual $f^{-1}(R)$ by step 2.1, so that it is Whitney-compatible with all previously emitted source strata. For each irreducible component $R_i$ of $R$, choose a dense smooth open $L_i\subseteq R_i$ as in step 1.1, respecting the target prescriptions and Whitney-regular with all previously emitted target strata. For every new source stratum $Z_\alpha$ compute the closure of its image in $R$; if that closure is not $R_i$, remove its intersection with $R_i$, a proper closed subset; if the closure is $R_i$, then $Z_\alpha\to R_i$ is dominant and [F4] supplies a dense open subset of $R_i$ on which the restriction is smooth and onto. Intersecting the finitely many resulting dense opens with $L_i$ gives a nonempty dense open $V_i\subseteq R_i$.

Emit the $V_i$ as target strata and the nonempty pieces $Z_\alpha\cap f^{-1}(V_i)$ as source strata. Each such piece is open in the smooth irreducible stratum $Z_\alpha$, hence smooth irreducible and locally closed, and it is Whitney-regular with every incident previously fixed upper source stratum, because Whitney conditions are local and were imposed on all of $Z_\alpha$ in step 2.1; with the pieces of the same round it has no frontier relation except through closures, which the later rounds make unions of strata because every closure is added to the respected list. Each piece maps smoothly and onto $V_i$ by its selection in step 3.1, and target strata are Whitney-regular with earlier target strata since $V_i\subseteq L_i$. Source frontier relations inside $f^{-1}(\bigcup_iV_i)$ are inherited from the source partition, and a stratum closure over $R_i$ misses every $V_j$ with $j\ne i$.

For local conical constructions one requires local properness over compact base slices: sufficiently small closed radius ranges over a compact neighbourhood in $R$ have compact inverse image inside the tube.

Only finitely many strata have closures not containing $y$; discard a small neighbourhood meeting none of those closures, so that only $R$ and its incident upper strata remain and $R$ is the lowest local stratum. Start the local induction of [F2] with this chosen $R$-tube, so that higher tubes preserve its projection and squared radius; all finite subsequent shrinks leave a positive uniform radius over the chosen compact base ball.

Put $W^\circ=X\cap\pi^{-1}(B)\cap\{0<r<\epsilon\}$ and $g=(\pi,r):W^\circ\to B\times(0,\epsilon)$. This map is a proper stratified submersion: a compact target subset lies over a compact base subset and a closed radial interval bounded away from zero and $\epsilon$, and its inverse image is a closed subset of a compact normal disk-bundle slice inside the chart where $X$ is closed. The upper tubes are $g$-compatible by the control equations of step 1.1. Fix $0<r_0<\epsilon/3$; the reference fibre $L_y=g^{-1}(y,r_0)$ is compact, being the intersection of $X$ with the affine normal space $y+N_yR$ and the radius-$r_0$ sphere. It is real semialgebraic: in this affine chart $X$ and its algebraic strata are described by finitely many real polynomial equalities and inequalities, and the normal plane and sphere have linear and quadratic equations.

By [F3] lift coordinate fields on $B$ preserving the radial coordinate; their flows trivialize the whole reference-radius link family over a smaller base box, identifying $g^{-1}(B\times\{r_0\})$ with $B\times L_y$. Separately lift the radial base field $r\partial_r$, cut off only near the upper radial endpoint so that it equals $r\partial_r$ for $r\le r_0$; properness of $g$ supplies all lifted finite-time transports between any two positive radii in $(0,r_0]$, with time $\log(r/r_0)$ and inverse of opposite time. These flows keep $\pi$ fixed, so combining horizontal reference-radius transport with radial transport gives a stratum-preserving homeomorphism $B\times L_y\times(0,r_0)\to X\cap\pi^{-1}(B)\cap\{0<r<r_0\}$ with continuous inverse. Commutation between different chosen lifts is unnecessary because the flows are applied and reversed in a fixed order.

Extend the map of step 3.1 over cone apex points by sending $(b,\mathrm{apex})$ to $b\in R$. The distance from a transported point to its base point is exactly its ordinary normal radius $r$, so convergence to the apex is uniform over the compact link and compact base subboxes independently of the speed of the radial field; conversely, $x_j\to b\in R$ gives $\pi(x_j)\to b$ and $r(x_j)\to0$, and compactness of $L_y$ means the radial parameters converge to the apex in its quotient cone topology regardless of the link direction. Hence both the extended map and its inverse are continuous, and the image $U_y=X\cap\pi^{-1}(B)\cap\{r<r_0\}$ is open in $X$. Rescaling $r$ identifies its radial interval with $[0,1)$, yielding the displayed ball times cone; if there are no upper strata the link is empty and its cone is the single apex.

The link strata are the intersections of the upper strata with the normal plane and sphere, and they are smooth by submersivity of $g$. They satisfy the frontier and Whitney conditions. For the frontier assertion, [F3] gives a source-local product for $g$ at each lower fibre point, so taking a stratum closure commutes locally with taking that fixed fibre, and the original frontier relations restrict with the same dimension drop in each stratum. Assume AC. Let $W\subseteq\mathbb R^N$ have a finite smooth Whitney (a),(b)
frontier stratification by locally closed embedded strata. There are tube
control data $(T_S,\pi_S,\rho_S)$, with $\rho_S$ a squared bundle radius, such
that incident overlap compositions are defined and satisfy
$\pi_R\pi_S=\pi_R$, $\rho_R\pi_S=\rho_R$ for $R<S$. Incomparable strata have
disjoint tubes, $(\pi_R,\rho_R)$ is a submersion on incident upper strata, and
the tube data have local properness over compact lower-stratum slices. If a
smooth ambient map $f$ is a submersion on every stratum, the tubes can
additionally satisfy $f\pi_S=f$. The statement is about compatible data;
continuous controlled flows are a separate construction.
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Every open cover of a smooth manifold admits a smooth partition of unity subordinate to it.

Let $F(t,x,\lambda)$ be jointly $C^\infty$ in $(t,x,\lambda)$ on an open time-state-parameter
domain. Near any base data $(t_0,x_0,\lambda_0)$ there are a compact time
interval $I$ and a neighbourhood $W$ of $(x_0,\lambda_0)$ such that, for every
$(y,\lambda)\in W$, the solution of

$$x'(t)=F(t,x(t),\lambda),\qquad x(t_0)=y,$$

is defined on $I$, and the resulting solution map is smooth in the pair
$(y,\lambda)$.

In ZF,

$$\mathrm{AC}\Longrightarrow\mathrm{DC}\Longrightarrow\mathrm{AC}_\omega\Longrightarrow\mathrm{AC}_{\omega,\mathrm{fin}}\Longrightarrow\mathrm{AC}_{\omega,2},\qquad \mathrm{AC}\Longrightarrow\mathrm{AC}_2.$$

DC here includes a prescribed initial point.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

The old identities survive: $\pi_Y\pi_X=\pi_Y$ shows that both the numerator and the positive base factor of the new $\rho_Y$ are preserved by $\pi_X$, and submersivity of $(\pi_X,\rho_X)$ survives because $(x,r)\mapsto(x,r/b_X(x)^2)$ is a diffeomorphism for positive $r$. Local properness survives over compact base slices, where $b_X$ has positive minimum and finite maximum. Use the closed middle bands $\rho_X\le1/2$ and inner bands $\rho_X<1/4$; their relative closures in higher strata lie inside the outer tube by the frontier-displacement bound of [F1], and incomparable tubes remain disjoint.

Fix $X$. On $W\cap T_X\setminus X$ the map $g_X=(\pi_X,\rho_X)$ is submersive on each stratum. Construct a field lifting the target field $(0,r)$ in increasing dimension of incident strata: on a minimal stratum use a smooth right inverse of $dg_X$ given by the adjoint minimum-norm matrix inverse; on a higher stratum inside a lower incident $Z$-tube lift $(V_Z\pi_Z,0)$ through $(d\pi_Z,d\rho_Z)$, which also lifts $(0,r)$ because $g_X\pi_Z=g_X$. The active middle-band controllers at any point form a chain by [F1], and the maximal one implies all lower constraints by differentiating the control factorizations. Patches avoiding inactive closed middle bands and lying inside the active outer domains, combined with a smooth subordinate partition (whose derivatives do not enter, since the equations in the field are linear), give a smooth field $V_X$ with $dg_XV_X=(0,\rho_X)$ and with $d\pi_ZV_X=V_Z\pi_Z$, $d\rho_ZV_X=0$ in every inner $Z$-band. Doing this for the finitely many $X$ with the same constant bands, then retaining only inner tubes and multiplying all radii by four, restores $\rho_Z<1$ on every retained tube by a constant rescaling that preserves all equations. For $Y<X$ the field also preserves $\pi_Y$ and $\rho_Y$ wherever defined, because both factor through $\pi_X$ and $d\pi_XV_X=0$.

Establish compact trapping for these fields, without assuming ambient boundedness on open strata, by induction on stratum dimension. Near a point $q$ of a lower stratum $Z$ choose a compact base slice $C\subseteq Z$ containing its trajectory for a common short time, and a closed small radius band whose inverse image $K$ is compact and lies inside the retained tube. For initial upper points close enough to $q$ the projected trajectory follows the smooth $Z$-flow and its radius stays constant, so while the upper ODE exists it remains in the interior of $K$: a first exit would have a compact limit with base in the interior of $C$ and radius strictly below the outer boundary, a contradiction. If an upper trajectory had a finite maximal endpoint within the common interval, compactness gives a cluster point; a cluster point in its own stratum allows ordinary ODE extension because the smooth field is bounded on a relatively compact coordinate ball and a sufficiently late visit cannot leave during the remaining short time, making the path Cauchy; a cluster point $q'$ in a lower stratum $Z'$ admits the same base-flow trap on a short interval covering the remaining time, and a sufficiently late visit to that trap cannot leave it, with $\rho_{Z'}$ a fixed positive value on the terminal segment, contradicting that the visits converge to $q'$ and force that value to zero; only incident lower strata can be cluster strata by the frontier condition. This gives a common short flow interval near each lower point, and the same argument backward gives inverse flows. Joint continuity follows from the compact tube slice estimate that the distance to the projection tends uniformly to zero as the radius tends to zero together with continuity of the projected lower flow, so incident-stratum sequences approaching a lower initial point have the correct flow limit; finite stratification and time subdivision complete the induction.

Obtain the initial radial family by flowing the field $V_X$ for time $\log(s/\rho_X(p))$, since $\dot\rho_X=\rho_X$ and $\dot\pi_X=0$; this time is finite and positive for positive source and target levels inside the retained domain, and existence over the fixed base $\pi_X(p)$ with radii in a closed positive interval follows because the full inverse image in compact $W$ is compact in normal-bundle coordinates, so step 3.1's endpoint argument applies. Ordinary uniqueness gives the semigroup identity and inverse transport between levels; the control equations give preservation of every other incident radius and projection, and of the higher-projection equivariance. A trajectory starting in a retained higher tube cannot leave it during a finite radial transport, because its normalized radius there is constant and a first exit is excluded by local properness over the compact projected trajectory; the same holds for transport in a lower tube across a higher tube. Consequently all transports used below stay in their actual normalized tube domains, which is the purpose of step 1.1's normalization.

Construct the final families in increasing dimension of $X$. Suppose the lower families are fixed and modify the current $X$-family by a decreasing induction on $Y<X$. For the currently processed $Y$ retain a small outer $Y$-band $0<\rho_Y<c$ lying inside all previously needed $Y$-commutation domains, possible with a positive constant by the finitely many earlier corrections, and put $a=c/2$. Writing $F^Y_{u\to v}$ for transport along the fixed $Y$-family between radius levels, choose a smooth $\phi$ with $\phi(t)=a$ for $t\le a$, $\phi(t)=t$ for $t\ge2c/3$, and $a\le\phi(t)<c$ for $0<t<c$. For a point $p$ with $t=\rho_Y(p)<c$ replace the current $X$-family by $\widetilde R_X(s)(p)=F^Y_{\phi(t)\to t}R_X(s)F^Y_{t\to\phi(t)}(p)$; all terms are defined by step 4.1, the intermediate $X$-operation preserves the $Y$-radius, the modification is conjugation on each fixed $Y$-slice and equals the old family near the outer boundary where $\phi(t)=t$, so it patches continuously and stratumwise smoothly with the old family outside the $Y$-band.

The correction preserves the $X$-semigroup law because both $X$-operations preserve $t$ and the middle $Y$-transports cancel; it preserves $\rho_X\widetilde R_X(s)=s$ because the $Y$-transports preserve $\rho_X$; it preserves $\pi_X$ because higher-projection equivariance of the $Y$-transports moves the $X$-base forward and back around an $X$-operation that fixes its base. For any other incident radius $\rho_Z$ each $Y$-transport preserves it and the middle $X$-operation preserves it, while for $Z=Y$ the two transports cancel its change. Lower-projection preservation and higher-projection equivariance survive by the same composition calculation: a $Y$-transport that moves such a projection has its equivariance move it forward and back around an $X$-operation fixing it, or produces the identical corrected operation on the projected higher stratum. Hence all domain statements and actual controls of step 4.1 remain true after the correction.

For $t<a$ the correction transports to the common reference level $a$, performs the same $X$-operation there and transports back, so in $Y$-coordinates $(q,t)=(R_Y(a)p,\rho_Y(p))$ it has the form $(q,t)\mapsto(A_s(q),t)$ independent of $t$; it therefore commutes with every $Y$-transport whose source and target lie in this inner band. Shrink the final $Y$-commutation domain to $t<a$ (retaining the outer maps for the next correction, and rescaling by the constant $a$ if desired). For a previously treated $Z$ with $Y<Z<X$ the $Z$-family commutes with the $Y$-transports by the fixed lower-family construction, preserves $t$, and commutes with the current $X$-family by the inner induction, so moving it through the three factors of step 5.1 shows it commutes with the corrected $X$-family. Incomparable strata have disjoint tubes and equal-dimensional strata are incomparable, so all previously imposed commutations survive; the finite nested induction terminates with every incident pair commuting, and all further rescalings are by constants that preserve radius equalities and controls.

Fix a retained normalized reference $a$. The inverse of $p\mapsto(R_X(a)p,\rho_X(p))$ is $(q,t)\mapsto R_X(t)q$, by the semigroup law and the invertible level transport of step 4.1; both maps are continuous and smooth on each incident stratum. Adjoining the zero end by $(q,0)\mapsto\pi_X(q)$ is continuous: locally on compact base slices the parameter-vector norm is $b_X(\pi_X(p))\sqrt{\rho_X(p)}$, the smooth tube embedding has bounded fibre derivative on a smaller compact parameter slice, so the physical displacement is at most a fixed constant times this norm, and transport to radius zero converges uniformly to the base projection; the same estimate gives inverse continuity at the adjoined stratum, and compactness of each closed link fibre supplies the uniform quotient neighbourhoods. This yields the claimed open mapping-cylinder model and completes all assertions.
