Assume AC. Let $X$ be a reduced quasi-projective complex algebraic variety with
a finite smooth complex algebraic Whitney stratification. Its analytic
stratified space admits compatible tube control data. At every point $y$ of a
stratum $R$ there is a stratum-preserving neighborhood homeomorphism
$$U_y\cong B^{2\dim_{\mathbb C}R}\times c_{<1}(L_y),$$
where $L_y$ is a compact finitely Whitney-stratified real semialgebraic normal
link. The ball times cone apex is $R\cap U_y$, and upper strata correspond to
their link strata times positive radius and the ball. The local construction
can preserve a chosen ordinary normal projection and radius at $R$. Links are
locally constant in stratified homeomorphism type along $R$. Proper stratified
algebraic submersions, with their actual analytic properness, have whole-fiber
local stratified bundle trivializations; local submersions have
source-neighborhood products. No compatible triangulation or finite
sheaf-cochain model is assumed or asserted here.

Assume AC. A compact finite controlled Whitney-stratified subset of a smooth
ambient space admits a finite triangulation of dimension at most the largest
real stratum dimension, compatible with every stratum closure and any
prescribed union of strata. Each open stratum is a union of open simplices. The
homeomorphism is smooth on the pieces within each stratum. The construction may
make the finitely many normal link-bundle projections between triangulated
compact stratum cores piecewise linear. It does not make an arbitrary algebraic
map globally simplicial. In particular it applies individually to
compactifications of quasi-projective complex varieties and to their compact
controlled links, once the stated Whitney/control hypotheses have been
supplied.

Let $K$ be a finite simplicial complex and let $\sigma$ be a nonempty simplex.
Let $\operatorname{lk}_K\sigma$ be the subcomplex of simplices $\tau$ disjoint
from $\sigma$ with $\sigma\cup\tau\in K$, and let $\operatorname{st}_K(\sigma)$
be the open star of $\sigma$
([[def-simplicial-subcomplex-star-closure-and-link]]). Then
$$\operatorname{st}_K(\sigma)\cong\operatorname{relint}|\sigma|\times c_{<1}(|\operatorname{lk}_K\sigma|),$$
where $c_{<1}(L)=(L\times[0,1))/(L\times\{0\})$ with the quotient topology, and
the cone on the empty space means a single apex. The homeomorphism takes each
simplex interior containing $\sigma$ to the product with the corresponding
link-simplex interior and positive radial coordinate; the simplex $\sigma$
itself maps to the apex. The link is compact and has finitely many simplices.
If $D\subseteq K$ is a subcomplex and $\sigma\notin D$, this star lies in
$|K|\setminus|D|$.

Assume AC. Let $(X,A)$ be a finite CW pair of dimension $d$, let $k$ be a field
and let $L$ be a $k$-vector-space local system with finite-dimensional fibres
([[def-local-system-of-r-modules-and-its-pullback]]). Then $H^q(X,A;L)$ is
finite-dimensional, vanishes for $q<0$ and $q>d$, and for every field extension
$k\subseteq k'$ the natural map is an isomorphism:
$$H^q(X,A;L)\otimes_k k'\cong H^q(X,A;L\otimes_k k').$$
The assertion holds separately on every component, including the empty pair.

Assume AC. Let $K$ be a finite simplicial complex, $D$ a subcomplex and $X=|K|\setminus|D|$. Let $P$ be the face poset of the open simplices of $K$ not in $D$, ordered by inclusion of faces. The exact realization of finite-dimensional covariant $k$-diagrams on $P$ induces a fully faithful functor into $D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(X))$, with essential image the complexes having bounded finite-rank locally constant cohomology on each open simplex. Ordinary and compact-support cohomology, ordinary Hom and internal derived Hom have bounded finite cochain models and commute with every coefficient field extension. For a local product projection $\operatorname{pr}:V\times F\to V$ with supplied finite deleted-boundary models, there is a natural local comparison $R\operatorname{pr}_*\operatorname{pr}^*B\simeq B\otimes_k C^*(F;k)$, taking the unit to $B\otimes(k\to C^*(F;k))$. This does not assert that an arbitrary algebraic map is simplicial.

Let $P$ be a finite nonempty poset, regarded as a category with one arrow $p\to q$ exactly when $p\le q$, and let $h$ be the largest number of strict inequalities in a chain of $P$. Let $\operatorname{Diag}_k(P)$ be the abelian category of covariant diagrams of $k$-vector spaces on $P$, i.e. the functor category of $k$-vector spaces indexed by $P$, with its cochain complexes as in [[def-cochain-complex-in-an-abelian-category]]. If $M$ is a bounded complex of diagrams in $\operatorname{Diag}_k(P)$ whose vector spaces are finite-dimensional and vanish outside internal degrees $[a,b]$, then the derived inverse limit $\mathbf R\lim M:=\mathbf R\operatorname{Hom}(\underline k,M)$ ([[def-derived-hom-in-the-bounded-setting]]) has a finite-dimensional cochain model concentrated in $[a,b+h]$. If $A,B$ are such complexes, concentrated in $[a,b]$ and $[c,d]$ respectively, then their derived Hom has a finite-dimensional cochain model concentrated in $[c-b,d-a+h]$. These models commute with every field extension. For the empty poset, the diagram sections and the derived Hom model are zero by convention.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

derivations.claim: By quasi-projectivity choose an algebraic locally closed embedding $X\hookrightarrow\mathbb P^N$. Its reduced projective closure $\overline X$ has $X$ as an open subset, and $B=\overline X\setminus X$ is closed algebraic. Take closures of the finitely many marked supports and the pieces of the given constructibility stratification. Apply [F1]'s finite stratification construction on $\overline X$, respecting these closed algebraic subsets and their finite locally closed differences. This gives a complex Whitney refinement on which every cohomology sheaf of $F$ stays finite-rank locally constant; passing to smaller smooth strata preserves local constancy. The compact analytic space $\overline X^{\mathrm{an}}$ embeds smoothly in a finite Euclidean space: send a projective line represented by $z\ne0$ to its Hermitian rank-one projector $zz^*/(z^*z)$. This is well-defined, injective, and smooth in the projective coordinate charts; its chart inverse recovers the ratios of the projector's nonzero column, so it is a smooth embedding. It is compact because it is the continuous image of the unit sphere. Its restricted algebraic Whitney strata satisfy the real smooth Whitney conditions used by [F2]. Apply [F2], including all chosen stratum unions. Let $K$ be the resulting finite complex and $D$ the subcomplex mapping onto $B$; one barycentric subdivision makes every marked subcomplex full if needed. Restricting the homeomorphism yields $X^{\mathrm{an}}\cong |K|\setminus|D|$ as claimed.

Every retained open simplex is contained in one original complex stratum. The cohomology of $F$ on it is finite-rank locally constant, so $F$ belongs to the actual essential image of [F4]. It therefore has a bounded finite-dimensional diagram representative on the face poset of the retained simplices, with no assertion that the analytic sheaf category itself is finite. The finite bar construction of [F5] computes actual ordinary derived global sections and actual derived Hom because [F4] proves full faithfulness against the analytic sheaf category by independently established star acyclicity. Its compact-support clause identifies the actual support functor with finite relative cochains on the compactification pair; this uses the c-soft acyclicity and open extension by zero declared in [F4]. Finite simplicial stars and their closed subcomplex complements admit the explicit finite product/cone models of [F3]. Thus local support cohomology is computed by the finite cone of restriction from such a neighborhood to its complement of the marked support, with the conventional shift determined by the support triangle. These restrictions and their maps are the actual sheaf restrictions under [F4], not merely vector spaces with matching dimensions. For the constant sheaf on a compact model the ordinary cellular model has no cochain terms above the simplicial dimension, which is at most twice the complex dimension by [F2]. All face-chain lengths and cohomology amplitudes are finite, so the models are uniformly bounded for the finitely many chosen strata and supports.

The ordinary incidence calculation alone gives constructibility on real simplices. To obtain local constancy along a complex stratum $S$, use [F1]'s actual local chart $U\cong V\times cL$, where $V$ is a small contractible ball in $S$ and the chart preserves the complex strata. The compact link $L$ has a finite inherited controlled stratification and a finite triangulation by [F2], and $cL$ truncated to a finite radius has a finite deleted-boundary model. Each product stratum is a product of the contractible $V$ with a link stratum. The restriction of the cohomology sheaves of $F$ is locally constant there. On a link simplex, therefore, its restriction to $V$ times that simplex is represented by a finite coefficient complex independent of the $V$ direction. This last derived assertion follows from [F4], rather than assuming a sheaf is invariant under every stratum-preserving homeomorphism: pullback along the projection to the link is fully faithful on the relevant finite incidence categories because [F4]'s product comparison has fibre $V$ and $C^*(V;k)\simeq k$ by [F3]. Filter the finitely many link simplices by closed skeleta. On a simplex piece the object is a pullback: finite-rank constant sheaves on the contractible product have no positive Ext between them by [F4] and its constant-sheaf comparison. The finite ordinary truncation triangles therefore split there, expressing its locally constant bounded complex by a finite coefficient complex. The ordinary exact open/closed extension-by-zero triangles in [F4] build the object through this finite filtration. Full faithfulness lifts the connecting morphisms between pullbacks, so their finite cones are again pullbacks. Induction proves that the restriction of $F$ to this chart is pulled back from a finite link-cone object. The same argument applies simultaneously to the chosen finite collection of input objects and marked support strata.

In step 3.1's chart, ordinary local sections, punctured-neighborhood sections and sections with a marked support are therefore the corresponding finite link/cone cochains, constant in the $V$ direction. Their restriction morphisms are the product/incidence morphisms, so their support cones are locally constant too. Applying this also to two input complexes shows that their internal derived Hom is locally constant in the $V$ direction, with bounded finite-dimensional stalks computed by [F4] and [F5]. Finitely many complex Whitney strata give a uniform amplitude bound. Hence the result is constructible for the complex stratification (or its finite simultaneous support refinement), not merely for the real simplex partition. This is the local constructibility and finite local cohomology assertion required for the later open/closed and perverse gluing constructions. It does not substitute the real simplex dimension for the complex dimension of $S$.

Finally every displayed incidence, bar, relative support and link-cone model is a finite matrix complex of finite-dimensional $k$-spaces. Tensor with a field extension $k\subset k'$ is exact, carries its kernels and images to the corresponding kernels and images, and commutes with every finite sum, differential, restriction map and cone. The comparisons of [F4] and the finite local-system comparison of [F3] therefore identify these scalar-extended complexes with the actual corresponding sheaf constructions over $k'$. The constructions and comparisons are locally coherent through their actual incidence morphisms. This proves all claimed finite cohomology and coefficient-extension assertions.

Assume AC. Let $f:X\to Y$ be one morphism of reduced quasi-projective complex
algebraic varieties, and prescribe finitely many closed or locally closed
algebraic subsets in source and target. There exist finite smooth complex
algebraic Whitney (a),(b) stratifications with frontier on $X$ and $Y$
respecting all prescribed subsets, such that each source stratum maps
surjectively and smoothly onto one target stratum. A further finite algebraic
stratification may be prescribed and refined. The analytic strata are smooth
complex manifolds and the restrictions are smooth submersions. If $f$ is proper
in the analytic topology, in particular if it is a projective algebraic
morphism, the whole restriction $f^{-1}(T)\to T$ over any target stratum is
proper; no restriction of $f$ to a nonclosed individual source stratum is
asserted proper.

Assume AC. Let $X$ be a reduced quasi-projective complex algebraic variety with
a finite smooth complex algebraic Whitney stratification. Its analytic
stratified space admits compatible tube control data. At every point $y$ of a
stratum $R$ there is a stratum-preserving neighborhood homeomorphism
$$U_y\cong B^{2\dim_{\mathbb C}R}\times c_{<1}(L_y),$$
where $L_y$ is a compact finitely Whitney-stratified real semialgebraic normal
link. The ball times cone apex is $R\cap U_y$, and upper strata correspond to
their link strata times positive radius and the ball. The local construction
can preserve a chosen ordinary normal projection and radius at $R$. Links are
locally constant in stratified homeomorphism type along $R$. Proper stratified
algebraic submersions, with their actual analytic properness, have whole-fiber
local stratified bundle trivializations; local submersions have
source-neighborhood products. No compatible triangulation or finite
sheaf-cochain model is assumed or asserted here.

Assume AC. Let $X$ be a quasi-projective complex algebraic variety, $k$ a
field, and $F$ a bounded complex of analytic $k$-sheaves whose cohomology is
locally constant of finite rank on a finite complex algebraic stratification.
Fix finitely many algebraic supports and locally closed inclusions to be
respected. There is a finite compatible smooth complex algebraic Whitney
refinement, a projective compactification with its algebraic boundary
respected, and a finite pair of simplicial complexes $(K,D)$ such that
$X^{\mathrm{an}}\cong|K|\setminus|D|$, every open simplex lies in one complex
stratum, and the marked supports are unions of simplices. One can take
$\dim K\le2\dim_{\mathbb C}X$; in particular constant-sheaf cohomology vanishes
above that real dimension. The same construction applies individually to the
compact controlled links supplied by the conical-neighborhood theorem.

On these models, actual ordinary and compact-support cohomology, ordinary
derived Hom, internal derived Hom and local cohomology with a prescribed
algebraic support have bounded finite-dimensional cochain models. Internal Hom
is constructible on a finite complex Whitney refinement. The local link and
support models vary locally constantly along the corresponding complex strata;
thus their cohomology has finite rank there. Every such model commutes with
extension of the coefficient field. Inclusions and supports are chosen in
finite collections for a given construction; no compatible triangulation of
arbitrary algebraic maps or cyclic diagrams is asserted. Perverse dimensions
remain the dimensions of the complex strata, independent of the auxiliary real
simplices.

Assume AC. Let $K$ be a finite simplicial complex, $D$ a subcomplex and $X=|K|\setminus|D|$. Let $P$ be the face poset of the open simplices of $K$ not in $D$, ordered by inclusion of faces. The exact realization of finite-dimensional covariant $k$-diagrams on $P$ induces a fully faithful functor into $D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(X))$, with essential image the complexes having bounded finite-rank locally constant cohomology on each open simplex. Ordinary and compact-support cohomology, ordinary Hom and internal derived Hom have bounded finite cochain models and commute with every coefficient field extension. For a local product projection $\operatorname{pr}:V\times F\to V$ with supplied finite deleted-boundary models, there is a natural local comparison $R\operatorname{pr}_*\operatorname{pr}^*B\simeq B\otimes_k C^*(F;k)$, taking the unit to $B\otimes(k\to C^*(F;k))$. This does not assert that an arbitrary algebraic map is simplicial.

Assume AC. For a strict augmented simplicial space $Z_\bullet\to S$, its category of simplicial analytic $k$-sheaves has explicit coinduced injective resolutions. The derived augmentation is computed by the normalized double complex with first page $R^j q_{p*}F_p$ and alternating face differential. A common internal lower bound makes every total-degree diagonal finite. The same construction works for strict bisimplicial diagrams and is compatible with composition of derived right adjoints to exact inverse image. If $Z_\bullet$ is the Čech nerve of a map $P\to S$ admitting local sections, inverse image gives an equivalence from $D^b(\operatorname{Sh}_k(S))$ to the full derived subcategory with Cartesian cohomology. For algebraic principal $\mathrm{GL}$ bundles this restricts to the algebraically constructible subcategories.

Let $k$ be a field and let $X,Y$ be locally compact Hausdorff spaces
([[def-locally-compact-space]], [[def-hausdorff-space]]). Write
$\operatorname{Sh}_k(X)$ for the category of sheaves of $k$-vector spaces
([[def-sheaf-on-topological-space]], [[def-sheaf-cohomology-derived-global-sections]])
viewed as modules over the constant ring sheaf $k_X$, and form derived
categories in those sheaves ([[def-derived-category-of-an-abelian-category]]).
For a continuous map $f:X\to Y$, set $f^*=f^{-1}$
([[def-inverse-image-presheaf-and-sheaf]]) and define $f_!F$ on an open
$V\subseteq Y$ to consist of the sections of $F$ on $f^{-1}(V)$ whose closed
support ([[def-support-of-a-sheaf-section]],
[[def-compactly-supported-global-sections]]) maps properly to $V$, properness
being that of [[def-proper-continuous-map]] together with its stability lemma
[[lem-proper-continuous-map-stability]]. Under AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]),
$Rf_*$ and $Rf_!$ are computed on bounded-below $k$-linear injective
replacements. Tensor means the signed total tensor over $k$
([[def-sheaf-tensor-product]]) and internal derived Hom is the injective
construction of
[[lem-bounded-analytic-field-sheaves-have-derived-tensor-hom-and-pullback-pushforward-adjunctions]]
([[def-sheaf-hom]]).

Suppose the uniform all-fibre-open cohomological dimension bound of
[[lem-finite-fibre-dimension-gives-bounded-fibrewise-soft-resolutions]] holds,
and choose its finite resolution $k_X\to K$; for an open $U\subseteq X$ put
$K_U=j_{U!}j_U^*K$ ([[def-extension-by-zero-abelian-sheaf]],
[[def-c-soft-sheaf]]). For a bounded-below injective complex $I$ on $Y$,
define the exceptional inverse-image candidate to be the sheaf complex with
open sections $\operatorname{Hom}_Y^\bullet(f_!K_U,I)$.
[[thm-compactly-supported-derived-pushforward-has-exceptional-inverse-image-adjoint]]
proves that this candidate is a sheaf complex and is independent of the chosen
resolution. Set $\omega_X=a_X^!k$ and $D_XA=R\mathcal Hom(A,\omega_X)$ when the
terminal map satisfies the same finite-dimensional hypotheses. Constructible
restriction is a separate geometric theorem; none of these definitions asserts
a generic six-functor axiom.

The prescriptions are those of Verdier's exposé: $f^*$ is the exact inverse
image, $f_!$ is the sheaf of sections whose closed support is proper over the
base — a presheaf by the local nature of properness, whose sheaf property on
bounded-below injective inputs is proved by the exceptional-adjoint theorem
recorded in `justified_by` — $Rf_*$ is derived from the direct image
[[def-direct-image-sheaf]] on bounded-below injective replacements, and the
terms of the chosen finite resolution are $c$-soft and hence acyclic for
compact support ([[lem-c-soft-field-sheaves-are-compact-support-acyclic]]).
The ordinary-operations lemma also supplies the flasque acyclicity
([[def-flasque-sheaf]]) used to compare resolutions. AC is used only for
injective replacements; the proper-support sections, extension by zero and the
exceptional candidate itself are choice-free constructions. Cohomological
shifts obey $H^i(A[r])=H^{i+r}(A)$ in the convention of
[[def-derived-category-of-an-abelian-category]].

Under the preceding locally compact and finite-dimensional hypotheses, $u^*Rf_!\simeq Rf'_!v^*$ for Cartesian squares; proper maps have $Rf_!=Rf_*$, giving proper ordinary base change. Bounded tensor factors satisfy the projection formula. Proper-support direct images compose canonically. On the bounded constructible specialization proved by the subsequent local duality construction, exceptional adjoints also compose canonically; their units, counits and traces respect composition and Cartesian pasting. For a closed inclusion $i:Z\to X$ with complement $j$, $i^!$ is the derived functor of $i^{-1}\Gamma_Z$, and both localization triangles hold. Locally, $R\mathcal Hom(i_*k_Z,A)$ is $R\Gamma_ZA$. This lemma does not assume or claim extraordinary dual base change before constructible biduality.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $P=|K|$ be the realization of a finite abstract
simplicial complex $K$ of dimension $d$ (a finite compact polyhedron of
dimension $d$), and let $\mathcal F$ be a sheaf of abelian groups on $P$
([[def-geometric-realization-of-an-abstract-simplicial-complex]],
[[def-locally-finite-and-finite-dimensional-simplicial-complex]],
[[def-sheaf-on-topological-space]]); every clause applies to sheaves of
$k$-vector spaces. Then:

1. $H^q(P,\mathcal F)=0$ for every $q>d$
   ([[def-sheaf-cohomology-derived-global-sections]]);
2. for every open subspace $U\subseteq P$ and every sheaf $\mathcal E$ of
   abelian groups on $U$, one has $H^q_c(U,\mathcal E)=0$ for every $q>d$
   ([[def-compactly-supported-global-sections]]);
3. more generally, the same conclusions hold for every compact Hausdorff space
   in which every open cover admits a finite open refinement of order at most
   $d+1$ --- that is, a finite refinement such that every point lies in at most
   $d+1$ of its members --- and for every open subspace of such a space.

These bounds concern arbitrary sheaves, not merely cellular, constructible or
coherent ones. If $L\subseteq K$ is a subcomplex, then $|L|$ is closed in $P$,
the complement $P\setminus|L|$ is open, and every open subspace of
$P\setminus|L|$ is an open subspace of $P$; this is the fibre model on which
the bound is applied.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

derivations.claim: For each individual quasi-projective map and support collection, apply the actual compatible-stratification and control suppliers, followed by their fixed-space triangulation supplier. This is the precise geometric scope actually authored upstream. On each supplied finite deleted-boundary model the incidence theorem proves the finite local/global cochains, internal-Hom constructibility and field-extension comparison. Choices for different operations need not form one jointly stratified cyclic diagram.

A separated finite-type variety has a finite affine-open cover, whose finite intersections are affine: its closed diagonal identifies each two-chart intersection with a closed subscheme of the affine chart product, and iterate. Each intersection is quasi-projective. Apply the local geometric/incidence construction there. The actual finite open-cover Cech derived augmentation assembles their cochains. Only finitely many intersection degrees occur, and the finitely many local cohomology bounds give a uniform finite total bound. Hence ordinary/global derived Hom and cohomology are bounded and finite, and their finite complexes commute with field extension. Compact-support models are assembled by the ordinary open/closed support resolution and the same finite local models. Internal Hom is locally computed on the finite affine cover and its bounds are uniform; its algebraic constructibility is local and a finite refinement of the locally closed support pieces globalizes it.

For one morphism between quasi-projective varieties, choose a locally closed embedding of its source into $\mathbb P^N$ and take the reduced closure of its graph in $\mathbb P^N\times Y$. The graph is locally closed, hence open in that closure; thus the map factors as an open inclusion $j:X\hookrightarrow\overline X$ followed by the projective projection $p:\overline X\to Y$. The closure is quasi-projective and $p$ is analytically proper by [F1]. Each algebraic fibre has a deleted-boundary model of dimension at most twice the source dimension by [F3]; [F6] therefore bounds compact-support cohomology of every sheaf on every fibre open by that same integer. Thus the support operations satisfy their required all-fibre-open hypothesis, rather than merely a bound for constructible coefficients. Choose [F1]'s one-map Whitney strata for $p$, respecting the boundary $\overline X\setminus X$ and the finite input supports. Extension by zero $j_!$ is exact; $Rj_*$ is locally computed by the ordinary sections on the open part of [F2]'s controlled link-cone chart, and [F3] and [F4] give the bounded finite, locally constant complex-stratum model and its actual restriction maps. The proper whole-fibre local trivializations of [F2] give, over a small ball in each target stratum, a product with a compact stratified fibre. The same derived product reconstruction used in [F3] identifies the constructible input there with a fibre object constant in the ball direction, so its pushforward is its finite fibre cochain complex constant along that ball. Finitely many target strata give a uniform amplitude bound; ordinary direct-image composition (inverse image is exact, so direct image preserves injectives) and the proper-support composition of [F6] show $Rp_*Rj_*$ and $Rp_*j_!$ compute $Rf_*$ and $Rf_!$ respectively. All models and comparisons commute with field extension by [F3] and [F4]. For a general separated finite-type map, work over an affine target chart, take a finite affine cover of its source preimage and finite intersections, and apply this construction to their finite disjoint union mapping to the target. Prescribe the needed supports in that one-map construction, obtaining one target stratification for the finitely many terms. The actual finite open-cover derived augmentation of [F5] then assembles ordinary pushforward; its extension-by-zero support resolution assembles proper-support pushforward. Thus the outputs are bounded algebraically constructible locally on the target and hence globally by a finite affine cover. This proof uses a constructed projective factorization on each quasi-projective piece and proper whole-fibre triviality, rather than inferring whole-fibre control from local source charts. No joint stratification of an arbitrary cyclic diagram is required.

If $K$ is a finite abstract simplicial complex, then its geometric realization
$|K|$ is compact and Hausdorff.

Let $(X, \mathcal{T}_X)$ and $(Y, \mathcal{T}_Y)$ be topological spaces and let
$f : X \to Y$ be a function. Continuity is as in [[def-continuous-map-top]],
injections, surjections and bijections as in
[[def-injection-surjection-bijection]].

- $f$ is an **open map** if $f[U]$ is open in $Y$ for every open $U \subseteq X$.
- $f$ is a **closed map** if $f[F]$ is closed in $Y$ for every closed
  $F \subseteq X$.
- $f$ is a **homeomorphism** if $f$ is a continuous bijection whose inverse
  $f^{-1} : Y \to X$ is also continuous. The spaces are **homeomorphic**, written
  $X \cong Y$, when a homeomorphism $X \to Y$ exists.
- $f$ is an **embedding** if $f$ is injective and the corestriction
  $f_0 : X \to f[X]$, $f_0(x) = f(x)$, is a homeomorphism onto $f[X]$ carrying
  the subspace topology inherited from $Y$ ([[def-subspace-topology-top]]).

**The inverse in the third clause exists because $f$ is a bijection**, and it is
the unique two-sided inverse ([[def-injection-surjection-bijection]]); no choice
principle is involved. Continuity of $f^{-1}$ is a genuine additional demand: a
continuous bijection need not be a homeomorphism, and this page records that
failure as a false statement with a two-point witness.

**Open, closed and homeomorphism are three different conditions.** A
homeomorphism is continuous by definition, but an open map need not be continuous
and a closed map need not be continuous; and continuity implies neither openness
nor closedness. An open map need
not be closed and a closed map need not be open, and Sierpinski space
$S = \{a,b\}$ with open point $b$ ([[def-standard-topologies]]) witnesses both
failures at once: the constant map $S \to S$ with value $b$ is open, since the
image of every nonempty set is the open set $\{b\}$, and is not closed, since the
image of the closed set $\{a\}$ is $\{b\}$, whose complement $\{a\}$ is not open;
the constant map with value $a$ is closed and not open by the same computation
read the other way. What is true
is that for a **continuous bijection** the three notions collapse: it is a
homeomorphism exactly when it is open, exactly when it is closed. That is proved
in the next item and is not assumed here.

**Topological properties.** A **property of topological spaces** is a condition
$P$ that is either true or false of each space. $P$ is a **topological property**
(one is also said to be *preserved by homeomorphism*, or *invariant*) when
$X \cong Y$ implies that $P(X)$ and $P(Y)$ have the same truth value. Since
$\cong$ is an equivalence relation on spaces — the identity is a homeomorphism,
inverses and composites of homeomorphisms are homeomorphisms, all three verified
in the next item — a topological property is exactly one that is constant on each
$\cong$-class.

**What a homeomorphism transports.** If $h : X \to Y$ is a homeomorphism then
$U \mapsto h[U]$ is a bijection from $\mathcal{T}_X$ onto $\mathcal{T}_Y$, with
inverse $V \mapsto h^{-1}[V]$: both maps are well defined because $h$ and
$h^{-1}$ are continuous, and they are mutually inverse because $h$ is a
bijection. So a homeomorphism is an isomorphism of the structure "a set together
with a distinguished family of subsets", and every notion defined from the open
sets alone — closed, closure, interior, boundary, dense, convergence of
sequences, continuity of maps into and out of the space — is carried across by
it. Anything defined from extra data, such as a metric or an order, is not, and
that distinction is exactly what the phrase *topological property* is for.

Let $(X, \mathcal{T}_X)$ and $(Y, \mathcal{T}_Y)$ be topological spaces
([[def-topological-space]]), let $f : X \to Y$ be a function and let $x \in X$.
Neighbourhoods are as in [[def-neighbourhood-top]].

$f$ is **continuous at $x$** if for every neighbourhood $V$ of $f(x)$ in $Y$ the
preimage $f^{-1}[V]$ is a neighbourhood of $x$ in $X$.

$f$ is **continuous** if it is continuous at every point of $X$.

**The same condition with open sets only.** $f$ is continuous at $x$ if and only
if for every open $V \subseteq Y$ with $f(x) \in V$ there is an open
$U \subseteq X$ with $x \in U$ and $f[U] \subseteq V$. Indeed, if $f$ is
continuous at $x$ and $V$ is such an open set, then $V$ is a neighbourhood of
$f(x)$, so $f^{-1}[V]$ is a neighbourhood of $x$ and contains an open $U \ni x$,
which satisfies $f[U] \subseteq V$. Conversely, given the displayed condition and
a neighbourhood $V$ of $f(x)$, fix open $V_0$ with $f(x) \in V_0 \subseteq V$ and
then open $U \ni x$ with $f[U] \subseteq V_0$; then $x \in U \subseteq f^{-1}[V_0] \subseteq f^{-1}[V]$,
so $f^{-1}[V]$ is a neighbourhood of $x$. Both forms are used below and are the
same statement written twice.

**Preimage, not image.** $f^{-1}[V] = \{\, x \in X : f(x) \in V \,\}$
is the preimage in the sense of [[def-injection-surjection-bijection]] and is
defined for every function, invertible or not; no inverse function is being
asserted to exist. Continuity is a condition on preimages throughout, and the
corresponding conditions on images define the *open* and *closed* maps of a later
item, which are different notions.

derivations.claim: The increasing open disks $\{z:|z|<n\}$ for positive integers $n$ cover $\mathbb C$, and no finite subfamily covers: a finite union of such disks is contained in the largest of them. Hence $\mathbb C$ is not compact, and by [F1] it is not homeomorphic to the realization of any finite simplicial complex.

Let $K$ be the boundary complex of the octahedron with vertices $\pm e_1,\pm e_2,\pm e_3$ and eight triangular faces, one for each choice of signs. Its realization is $\{x\in\mathbb R^3:|x_1|+|x_2|+|x_3|=1\}$: every listed triangular face satisfies the equation and every point of the $\ell^1$-sphere lies in such a face. The radial normalization $x\mapsto x/\|x\|_2$ maps this realization bijectively onto the unit sphere $S^2$, with inverse $u\mapsto u/(|u_1|+|u_2|+|u_3|)$; both maps are continuous, so by [F2] it is a homeomorphism. Deleting the subcomplex consisting of the single vertex $e_3$ identifies $|K|\setminus\{e_3\}$ with $S^2\setminus\{e_3\}$.

For $(a,b)\in\mathbb R^2$ put $s=a^2+b^2$ and map $(a,b)$ to $(2a,2b,s-1)/(s+1)$. Its squared Euclidean norm is $(4s+(s-1)^2)/(s+1)^2=(s+1)^2/(s+1)^2=1$, so the image lies on $S^2$, and its third coordinate $(s-1)/(s+1)$ is strictly less than $1$. The map $u\mapsto(u_1,u_2)/(1-u_3)$ is defined on $S^2\setminus\{e_3\}$ and is inverse to the previous formula by direct substitution; both are continuous.
